claim: Article 19(1)(d) and (e): all citizens have the right 'to move freely throughout the territory of India' and 'to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India'. The right is given to citizens only.
source: Constitution of India as on 10 Sep 2026, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
page_or_section: Art. 19(1)(d) PDF p.40; (e) PDF p.41 (printed p.10)
note: Ledger POL03-D01 gives the list of six freedoms; this row names (d) and (e). Sub-clause (f) (property) was omitted by the 44th Amendment (w.e.f. 20-6-1979), so after 1979 clause (5) covers only (d) and (e) (footnote 5, PDF p.41).

claim: Article 19(5): nothing in sub-clauses (d) and (e) affects any existing law, or stops the State making a law, imposing reasonable restrictions on those rights 'either in the interests of the general public or for the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe'.
value: two grounds: general public; Scheduled Tribe interests
source: Constitution of India as on 10 Sep 2026, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
note: Same text as ledger POL03-D03. Re-read 10 Nov 2026 in the local Legislative Department text (research/upsc/POL-06/sources/leg_constitution_sep2026.txt, line 1392): 'either in the interests of the general public or for the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe'. The words 'sub-clauses (d) and (e)' replaced '(d), (e) and (f)' by the 44th Amendment (footnote 5). Restrictions must be 'reasonable': courts test them (claims -05 to -08).

claim: Article 358(1): while a Proclamation of Emergency declaring that the security of India is threatened by war or external aggression is in operation, nothing in Article 19 restricts the State's power to make laws or take executive action; such laws lapse when the Proclamation ceases.
value: Art 19 (including 19(1)(d),(e)) suspended only in a war/external-aggression Emergency
source: Constitution of India as on 10 Sep 2026, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
note: Article 359 (ledger POL03-D23) suspends the right to move courts; Article 358 is the one that suspends Article 19 itself. Text read as printed; the amendment history of the bracketed words was not traced.

claim: Article 16(2) bars discrimination or ineligibility in State employment on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence; Article 16(3) lets Parliament by law prescribe a residence requirement within a State or Union territory for employment under it.
value: 16(2) residence not a ground; 16(3) Parliament may require residence
source: Constitution of India as on 10 Sep 2026, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice
note: Shows another limit on residence-based rights: the Constitution itself lets Parliament (not the States) make residence a qualification for State jobs. Ledger POL03-B08 covers 16(1)-(2).

claim: Satwant Singh Sawhney v D. Ramarathnam (10 Apr 1967; five judges, 3:2: Subba Rao CJ, Shelat and Vaidialingam JJ. for the majority, Hidayatullah and Bachawat JJ. dissenting): the majority held that the expression 'personal liberty' in Art 21 takes in the right to travel abroad; the right to move throughout India is not covered by Art 21 because Art 19(1)(d) deals with it; no law regulated passports, so refusing one fell short of Art 21; the majority also held the refusal offended Art 14.

source: Satwant Singh Sawhney v D. Ramarathnam, 1967 2 SCR 525, via Indian Kanoon

source: Anuradha Bhasin v Union of India, via Indian Kanoon

claim: COVID-19 lockdown: on 24 Mar 2020 the National Disaster Management Authority issued an order under s.6(2)(i) of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and the Ministry of Home Affairs an order under s.10(2)(l), directing social distancing measures across the country for 21 days from 25 Mar 2020.

claim: Inner Line Permit (Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873; Reg. 5 of 1873): Indian citizens need a permit to enter parts of the North-East, justified by protecting tribal culture and land; which States are covered differs between Home Ministry replies of 2019 and 2020 (Manipur, Dimapur).
source: Ministry of Home Affairs, Lok Sabha replies 23 Jul 2019 and 11 Feb 2020

What is confirmed at an official source is claim -17 (Citizenship Act s.6B(4) names the Inner Line notified under the Regulation). Keep this row unsupported beyond -17; do not name States or sections.

claim: Article 19 freedoms belong to citizens only: foreigners and refugees cannot claim Art 19(1)(d) and (e); they have Art 21 and Art 14.
source: Constitution Art 19 ('All citizens'); Art 14 ('any person'); Art 21 ('No person')
note: Textually supported by ledger POL03-A10, A11 and L10 (CONFIRMED there); no case on non-citizens' movement was verified in this pass (Khudiram Chakma, 27 Apr 1993, was downloaded but the passage found is counsel's submission, not the holding). Cite the Articles, not the case.

claim: The Citizenship Act, 1955, s.6B(4) says that nothing in s.6B applies to the Sixth Schedule tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram or Tripura 'and the area covered under The Inner Line notified under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873 (Reg. 5 of 1873)'. So the Inner Line is a legal line notified under that 1873 Regulation, and Parliament recognised it in 2019.
value: Inner Line notified under Reg. 5 of 1873 (Citizenship Act s.6B(4))
source: India Code, The Citizenship Act, 1955, section 6B (Ministry of Home Affairs)
note: Read through India Code's data service on 2026-11-10. It establishes the Regulation as the legal basis of the Inner Line, but does not give the Regulation's own sections or the list of areas. The Act is a limiting provision for CAA citizenship, not a movement rule.
